title: Quantum Sampling, Expectation, and Monte Carlo

items.title: Finite expectation-estimation task
items.statement:
A **finite expectation-estimation task** consists of a nonempty finite set $X$, a probability law $p:X\to[0,1]$ with $\sum_{x\in X}p_x=1$, and an exactly encoded real-valued function $g:X\to[a,b]$, where $a\le b$ are finite rationals. Its target is
$$\mu:=\mathbb E_p[g]=\sum_{x\in X}p_xg(x).$$

For rational parameters $\varepsilon>0$ and $0<\delta<1$, an $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ estimator is a randomized or quantum procedure that outputs a real number $\widetilde\mu$ satisfying
$$\Pr\bigl(|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le\varepsilon\bigr)\ge1-\delta.$$
The task specifies the target law and success event only. A particular procedure must state how it accesses samples or coherent state preparation and must charge those resources separately.

A value that approximates an underlying real-valued observable to error $\tau$ defines a different task with target $\mathbb E_p[\widetilde g]$; any claim about $\mathbb E_p[g]$ must add the encoding error $\tau$ to its error budget.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 1–2
C. M. Grinstead and J. L. Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd ed., Sections 1.2 and 6.1

items.title: One-sided concentration bound for independent median trials
items.statement:
Let $R\ge1$ be an integer, let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_R$ be independent Bernoulli random variables on a finite probability space with $\mathbb E[Z_i]\le p<1/2$, and put $S=\sum_{i=1}^RZ_i$. For every $t\ge0$,
$$\Pr(S-\mathbb E S\ge t)\le e^{-2t^2/R}.$$
Consequently, let $R$ be odd and let $T_1,\ldots,T_R$ be independent finite-valued real estimates on a finite probability space. If $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an interval and $\Pr(T_i\in I)\ge1-p$ for every $i$, then their median (the middle order statistic) lies in $I$ except with probability at most
$$\exp\bigl(-2R(1/2-p)^2\bigr).$$

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Lemma 1 and Theorems 3 and 5
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; only a finite family of independent Bernoulli variables is considered.

items.title: Rational natural-logarithm enclosure search

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, Section 5.4.1 (analytic logarithm interface)

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; each iteration uses exact rational arithmetic.
items.statement:
**Input.** Rational numbers $x>0$ and $\tau>0$. **Output.** A positive integer $N$ and a rational interval $[L,U]$.

Compute $y=(x-1)/(x+1)$ and initialize $N=1$. At each iteration compute, by exact rational arithmetic,
$$S_N=2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{y^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad T_N=\frac{2|y|^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-y^2)}.$$
If $T_N\le\tau$, return $N$ and $[L,U]=[S_N-T_N,S_N+T_N]$. Otherwise replace $N$ by $N+1$ and repeat. Each comparison is an exact rational comparison. Arithmetic and integer bit costs are charged separately; no running-time bound is part of this definition.

items.title: A terminating rational enclosure for the natural logarithm
items.statement:
For a rational $x>0$, put $y=(x-1)/(x+1)$. For each integer $N\ge1$, define the rational partial sum and remainder bound
$$S_N(x):=2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{y^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad T_N(x):=\frac{2|y|^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-y^2)}.$$
Then $|y|<1$ and
$$|\ln x-S_N(x)|\le T_N(x).$$
For every rational tolerance $\tau>0$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-enclosure]] terminates using rational comparisons. It returns the certified interval $[S_N(x)-T_N(x),S_N(x)+T_N(x)]$, whose width is at most $2\tau$ and which contains $\ln x$.

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.100B Real Analysis, Spring 2025 full lecture notes
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, Logarithm and Exponential

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the construction uses finite rational arithmetic and a terminating natural-number search.

items.title: Finite termination of the dyadic estimator parameter searches
items.statement:
Let $a>0$ and $C>0$ be rational and let $k\ge1$ be an integer. Each of the following exact rational searches terminates:

1. increase an integer $j\ge0$ until $2^j a\ge1$;
2. after fixing $k$, increase an integer $m\ge0$ until $2^{2m}a^2\ge Ck$.

The first successful exponent is the least one satisfying its comparison. The second returns the least power of two $M=2^m$ with $M^2a^2\ge Ck$.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I
T. Tao, Analysis I, 3rd ed.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the witnesses are obtained by one Archimedean bound and a finite search.

items.title: Classical bounded-sample mean baseline
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite real random variable taking values in a finite interval $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent copies of $G$, with $n\ge1$. For $\overline X_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$ and $\mu=\mathbb E[G]$,
$$\mathbb E[\overline X_n]=\mu,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\overline X_n)=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(G)}{n}\le\frac{(b-a)^2}{4n}.$$
Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\Pr(|\overline X_n-\mu|>\varepsilon)\le\frac{(b-a)^2}{4n\varepsilon^2}.$$
The procedure uses exactly $n$ independent samples. If each draw and data load costs $C_{\rm draw}$ and $C_{\rm load}$, their total is $n(C_{\rm draw}+C_{\rm load})$; arithmetic for the encoded values is an additional separately charged cost. When $a=b$, every sample equals $\mu=a$ and the failure probability is zero.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Section 1
C. M. Grinstead and J. L. Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd ed., Sections 1.2 and 6.1
J. Matoušek and J. Vondrák, The Probabilistic Method, Lemma 5.1.3

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; only finite sums, finite samples, and their declared independence occur.

items.title: Uniform counting is finite indicator expectation
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set with $p_x=1/|X|$ for each $x$, let $S\subseteq X$, and define $g(x)=1$ for $x\in S$ and $g(x)=0$ otherwise. Then the expectation task for $(X,p,g)$ has target
$$\mu=\mathbb E[g]=\frac{|S|}{|X|}.$$

references.title: Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the sample space and all sums are finite.

items.title: Coherent finite sampler and observable value
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_{x\in X}p_x=1$, and let the value register contain an exact finite encoding of a real function $g:X\to[a,b]$, where $a\le b$ are finite rationals. A **coherent finite sampler** for $(X,p,g)$ is an explicitly supplied finite-dimensional unitary $V$ on ordered sample, value, and work registers such that
$$V|0\rangle=\sum_{x\in X}\sqrt{p_x}\,|x\rangle|g(x)\rangle|w_x\rangle,$$
where the sample labels $|x\rangle$ are distinct computational-basis vectors and each work state $|w_x\rangle$ has norm one. Zero-probability labels may occur and need no special branch. The registers and their order use [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] and [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]; each output is a pure state in the sense of [[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]]. The separate item [[lem-qa-29-coherent-sampler-outcome-law]] verifies the induced measurement law.

The access contract lists the actual circuits or oracle interfaces for $V$, $V^\dagger$, controlled $V$ and controlled $V^\dagger$, value decoding, reversible arithmetic, any coherent predicate and controlled rotation, and the reflections used by the chosen estimator. Their availability is explicit under [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]]. A forward unitary alone does not grant an inverse or a controlled call.

The resource record follows [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]: charge state preparation, inverse and controlled access, data loading, value comparison and arithmetic, controlled-rotation synthesis and precision, good-state and initial-state reflections, gates, width, ancillas, and classical postprocessing separately. The state-preparation circuit and its costs are inputs; a state description is not a free QRAM or preparation oracle.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 2–3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.title: Measurement law of a coherent sampler
items.statement: For a coherent sampler $V$ with output state $|\psi\rangle=\sum_x\sqrt{p_x}|x\rangle|g(x)\rangle|w_x\rangle$ as in [[def-qa-29-coherent-sampler]], projective measurement of the sample register returns $x$ with probability $p_x$. If the value register is measured too, the pair $(x,g(x))$ has the same probability. The work register is not required to be measured, and work states for different labels need not be orthogonal.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 2–3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Sections 2.1–2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3: Foundations II: Measurement and Evolution

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite orthonormal bases and finite sums.

items.title: Quantum counting as an expectation special case
items.statement:
**Input.** A Boolean domain $X=\{0,1\}^n$ with $N=2^n$, a predicate $f:X\to\{0,1\}$, a phase-register size $M=2^m$ for an integer $m\ge2$ (so $M\ge4$), and the uniform coherent access and controlled membership reflection required by [[alg-qa-13-counting-from-amplitude-estimation]]. Let $S=\{x:f(x)=1\}$.

Use the unchanged QA13 counting estimator [[alg-qa-13-counting-from-amplitude-estimation]] with this $M$ and its supplied access model, and return its exact algebraic fraction estimate $\widetilde\mu=\widetilde t/N=\sin^2(\pi y/M)$ for the expectation task. Its real-valued count estimate $\widetilde t=N\widetilde\mu$ may also be reported, with count and expectation outputs explicitly distinguished. Do not round to an integer unless that additional postprocessing and its cost are explicitly requested. By [[thm-qa-29-counting-is-indicator-expectation]], this is the QA29 expectation task for the uniform law and observable $g=\mathbf 1_S$; the applicable count guarantee is [[thm-qa-13-counting-error-guarantee]], whose phase-size hypothesis $M\ge4$ is met. Divide its count-error radius by $N$ for the expectation-error radius, with the same success event and probability. This item defines no second amplitude-estimation or counting routine.

references.title: Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.title: Amplitude-estimation expectation estimator
items.statement:
**Input.** A finite expectation-estimation task with an exact encoded observable $g:X\to[a,b]$, a coherent sampler $V$ for its law, rational target $\varepsilon>0$, and rational failure probability $0<\delta<1$. For $a<b$, require $\varepsilon\le b-a$. The supplied access model must include every forward, inverse, controlled, value, predicate, and reflection operation that the chosen QA13 amplitude-estimation circuit invokes.

If $a=b$, return $a$. Otherwise compute the exact affine value
$$q(x)=\frac{g(x)-a}{b-a}\in[0,1].$$
Append a good flag to the coherent sampler. Reversibly compute $q(x)$ in the declared value workspace, apply the supplied one-qubit rotation
$$|0\rangle\longmapsto\sqrt{1-q(x)}|0\rangle+\sqrt{q(x)}|1\rangle$$
controlled by the sample/value registers, and uncompute all scratch used only for $q$. Let $A_q$ denote the resulting state-preparation unitary, including $V$ and the controlled rotation; let $P_{\rm good}$ project onto flag $|1\rangle$. Run the unchanged median-confidence estimator [[alg-qa-13-median-confidence-estimation]] on $(A_q,P_{\rm good})$ with amplitude tolerance $\eta=\varepsilon/(b-a)$ and failure probability $\delta$, and call its estimate $\widetilde q$. Return
$$\widetilde\mu=a+(b-a)\widetilde q.$$

For $a=b$, the exact-return branch has no quantum call. When $a<b$, the input is a costed finite circuit/oracle description. Charge each use of $A_q$, $A_q^\dagger$, controlled versions, the good and initial-state reflections, value decoding, reversible arithmetic and uncomputation, the controlled rotation and its precision, phase estimation, state preparation, gates, width, ancillas, and classical output processing according to [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. No operation is free because it is described by the law $p$ or observable $g$.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Theorem 3
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.title: Variance-aware quantum Monte Carlo
items.statement:
**Input.** A coherent finite sampler $V$ whose decoded real output $v$ has finite range, a known rational upper bound $\sigma\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Var}(v)\le\sigma^2$, rational target $\varepsilon>0$, and rational desired failure probability $0<\rho<1$. All sample, value, inverse, controlled, predicate, and rotation circuits are explicit inputs with separately recorded costs. [[lem-qa-29-coherent-sampler-outcome-law]] identifies the distribution of each measured output with the sampler law. Every observable supplied to $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ is computed on fresh executions of $V$ using its explicitly supplied, costed value, predicate, rotation, inverse, and controlled operations. For an observable depending on a previously measured classical value, the input supplies the corresponding circuits for each admissible value and charges their selection or computation; the measured value is held fixed while those circuits are used.

If $\sigma=0$, measure one fresh output and return it. Otherwise set $\varepsilon'=\min(\varepsilon,\sigma/2)$ and reserve $\varepsilon_0=7\varepsilon'/8$ for the ideal estimator. Define the following finite routine for any nonnegative finite-valued output $h$ and rational parameters $a,\rho_1$ with $0<a<1/2$ and $0<\rho_1<1$:

1. Let $k$ be the least nonnegative integer with $2^ka\ge1$, and let $M=2^m$ be the least power of two, with $m\ge0$ an integer, for which $M^2a^2\ge10^6k$. Their exact rational searches terminate by [[lem-qa-29-dyadic-parameters-terminate]]. Moreover $k\ge2$ because $2a<1$; since $Ma\ge0$ and $(Ma)^2\ge10^6k$, [[thm-of-square-roots]] and [[lem-of-square-monotone]] give $Ma\ge1000\sqrt{k}$, hence $M\ge1000\sqrt{k}/a>2000$.
2. For $\ell=0$, define $h_0=h\mathbf1_{[0,1)}$. For $1\le\ell\le k$, define $h_\ell=2^{-\ell}h\mathbf1_{[2^{\ell-1},2^\ell)}$. Each $h_\ell$ lies in $[0,1)$.
3. Since $M>2000$, the target $\eta_M=88/(7M)$ satisfies $0<\eta_M<1$ and $M\ge4$. For each $\ell=0,\ldots,k$, run [[alg-qa-29-quantum-expectation-estimation]] on $h_\ell$ over $[0,1]$ with target $\eta_M$ and failure probability $1/[10(k+1)]$. This selects phase-register size exactly $M$ under the current QA13 interface. Call the result $u_\ell$ and form $P(h)=u_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^k2^\ell u_\ell$.
4. Repeat this whole binned procedure an odd number $R_1$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_1$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil2U_1/(3/10)^2\rceil+1$. Here $U_1$ is the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho_1)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Return the median. This defines $\operatorname{PositiveMean}(h,a,\rho_1)$ for $0<\rho_1<1$.

For one outer trial, measure one fresh sampler output $v_0$ and set $m=v_0/\sigma$. Holding this coarse value fixed, let $Y=v_1/\sigma$ be the normalized output of a new sampler execution independent of the coarse measurement and define
$$B_m(Y)=Y-m,\qquad h_{-,m}(Y)=(-B_m(Y))\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)<0}/4,\qquad h_{+,m}(Y)=B_m(Y)\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)\ge0}/4.$$
Run $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ separately on $h_{-,m}$ and $h_{+,m}$ with $a=\varepsilon_0/(32\sigma)$ and $\rho_1=1/9$, using fresh sampler executions independent of the coarse measurement and of the other call, conditional on the fixed $m$. If the results are $u_-,u_+$, return $\sigma(m-4u_-+4u_+)$. Count the coarse state preparation and all fresh preparations used by both $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ calls in the total preparation count; every controlled or inverse call remains separately charged. Let $U_0$ be the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Repeat the outer trial an odd number $R_0$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_0$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil18U_0\rceil+1$, and output the median.

Here $\ln$ is the natural logarithm from [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Its rational subroutine uses [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]] with tail at most $1/8$, yielding an interval of width at most $1/4$; every ceiling uses the interval's upper endpoint. The procedure is a finite sequence of operations in the supplied exact-access model, and the accuracy theorem assumes exact value, predicate, rotation, and reflection operations. It makes no guarantee for approximate replacements: any finite-gate implementation needs a separate certified error analysis that transfers both output accuracy and success probability, with compilation, gate, precision, bit, and ancilla costs recorded. No state reflection or value-loading operation is free.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Algorithms 1–3 and Theorems 3 and 5
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4

items.title: Quantum bounded-expectation guarantee and query cost
items.statement:
Let $g:X\to[a,b]$ be exactly encoded with $a\le b$, let $V$ be the coherent sampler of [[def-qa-29-coherent-sampler]], and let $\mu=\sum_xp_xg(x)$. If $a=b$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-quantum-expectation-estimation]] returns $a=\mu$ exactly. If $a<b$, then for rational $0<\varepsilon\le b-a$ and $0<\delta<1$ it returns $\widetilde\mu$ with $|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. Writing $q=(\mu-a)/(b-a)$ and $M$ for its QA13 phase-register size, the median output also obeys
$$|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le(b-a)\left(\frac{2\pi\sqrt{q(1-q)}}{M}+\frac{\pi^2}{M^2}\right)$$
with probability at least $1-\delta$ in either declared QA13 access mode. For $a<b$, in repeated controlled-$Q$ access it uses exactly $r(M-1)$ controlled-Grover calls, where $M$ and $r$ are the current QA13 median-interface parameters. In this mode its controlled-sampler/reflection query count is $O\bigl((b-a)\varepsilon^{-1}(1+\ln(1/\delta))\bigr)$ for all $0<\delta<1$, and $O\bigl((b-a)\varepsilon^{-1}\ln(1/\delta)\bigr)$ when $0<\delta\le1/2$. If $a=b$, the algorithm returns $a$ exactly with no quantum query.

For $a<b$, in supplied controlled-power access it instead uses exactly $rm$ controlled-power queries, where $M=2^m$; sum their separately declared costs over all $r$ runs. No $M-1$ constituent-call expansion is inferred for a supplied power.

The query bound is an oracle statement. Every controlled or inverse sampler call, good-state reflection, initial-state reflection, rotation, arithmetic operation, state preparation, and classical order-statistic computation retains its separately supplied cost.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Theorem 3
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Theorem 12
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all sample laws and phase registers are finite.

items.title: Dyadic positive-mean estimator under an L2 bound
items.statement:
Let $h$ be a nonnegative finite-valued output of a coherent sampler, $s=\|h\|_2=(\mathbb E[h^2])^{1/2}$, and let $a,\rho_1$ be rational with $0<a<1/2$ and $0<\rho_1<1$. Let $\operatorname{PositiveMean}(h,a,\rho_1)$ be the subroutine defined in [[alg-qa-29-variance-aware-monte-carlo]]. Its output $u$ satisfies
$$|u-\mathbb E[h]|\le a(1+s)^2$$
with probability at least $1-\rho_1$. For $k=\lceil\log_2(1/a)\rceil$, its calls use
$$O\bigl(k\ln(k+1)(1+\ln(1/\rho_1))\bigr)$$
prepared output-state copies and
$$O\bigl(a^{-1}k^{3/2}\ln(k+1)(1+\ln(1/\rho_1))\bigr)$$
uses of the supplied state reflection when its binned QAE calls use repeated controlled-$Q$ access. The accuracy and prepared-copy bounds also hold in supplied controlled-power access; in that mode sum the separately declared power-query costs rather than infer this reflection count. All input access, band comparison, value arithmetic, controlled rotation, and finite-precision costs remain separately charged.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Algorithm 2 and Lemma 4
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Theorem 12

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the bins, samples, and median repetitions are finite.

items.title: Variance-aware quantum Monte Carlo guarantee
items.statement:
Let $v$ be the finite-valued real output of a coherent sampler with $\operatorname{Var}(v)\le\sigma^2$ for a known rational $\sigma\ge0$, and let rational $\varepsilon>0$. For each rational $0<\rho<1$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-variance-aware-monte-carlo]] returns $\widetilde\mu$ with $|\widetilde\mu-\mathbb E[v]|\le\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\rho$. If $\sigma=0$, it returns the exact mean after one output preparation. For $\sigma>0$, put $z=\sigma/\varepsilon$ and $L=\max(2,z)$. In the exact coherent-access model, its resource counts are
$$O\!\left((1+\ln(1/\rho))\ln L\,\ln\ln(e^e+L)\right)$$
output-state preparations and
$$O\!\left((1+\ln(1/\rho))L(\ln L)^{3/2}\ln\ln(e^e+L)\right)$$
uses of the supplied state reflection in repeated controlled-$Q$ access, up to universal constants. Accuracy and the preparation bound hold in either declared access mode; in supplied controlled-power access sum the separately declared power costs instead of applying this reflection bound. Each state reflection is implemented through the supplied sampler and its inverse; these bounds do not turn variance alone into coherent access. A finite-gate approximation needs a separate certified error analysis before it can inherit this theorem.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Algorithm 3 and Theorem 5
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Theorem 12

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all random variables have finite range and all repetitions are finite.

items.title: Coherent query-to-circuit cost translation
items.statement:
For a QA29 execution, group its complete value-rotated sampler preparations into the distinct supplied unitaries $A_j$, and let $N_j$ be the number of fresh standalone preparations of $A_j$ and $Q_j$ the number of controlled Grover rounds using it. Also let $V_t$ range over the supplied unrotated sampler preparations used for coarse measurements, with $N_t^0$ such fresh preparations. If each controlled Grover round for $A_j$ is the explicit product of one controlled $A_j$ call, one controlled $A_j^\dagger$ call, one controlled initial-state reflection, one controlled good-state reflection, and its control phase, then the exact primitive-call cost is
$$\sum_jN_jC_{A_j,\rm prep}+\sum_tN_t^0C_{V_t,\rm prep}+\sum_jQ_j(C_{A_j,c}+C_{A_j^\dagger,c}+C_{S_{0,j},c}+C_{S_{{\rm good},j},c}+C_{{\rm phase},j}),$$
where every $C$ is the declared cost of that operation. The preparation counts exclude the controlled $A_j$ and $A_j^\dagger$ occurrences inside Grover rounds, which are already included in the $Q_j$ terms. With a single $A_q$, no unrotated coarse preparations, and $N_{\rm prep}=N_q$, this reduces to the homogeneous formula $N_{\rm prep}C_{A_q,\rm prep}+Q(C_{A_q,c}+C_{A_q^\dagger,c}+C_{S_0,c}+C_{S_{\rm good},c}+C_{\rm phase})$. Value decoding, band comparisons, reversible arithmetic, controlled rotations, uncomputation, phase estimation, ancilla workspace, circuit description, and classical output/median computations add their own declared gate, width, bit, or oracle costs. If a complete reflection is instead supplied as a named oracle, charge that oracle's declared cost separately and do not also expand it into its components. No bare query bound becomes a gate bound without these implementations.

references.title: Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Theorems 3 and 5

items.statement: A classical interface that returns independent samples from a finite law, by itself, supplies a coherent unitary sampler together with its inverse, controlled calls, value computation, and state reflections at no additional cost.

items.statement: Let $X\in\{0,1\}$ have $\Pr(X=1)=p$ and use $g(X)=X$ on the range $[0,1]$. Suppose a coherent sampler for this law and its explicitly costed inverse/controlled operations are supplied.
